item.title: 83% of nursing home residents vaccinated as flu surge hits
item.description: Around 83 per cent of nursing home residents have been vaccinated against flu. It comes as a flu surge hits many hospitals across the country. Visiting restrictions are in place at a number of hospitals nationwide to try and stop the virus from spreading. Advertisement Nursing Homes Ireland Chief Executive, Tadhg Daly says nursing homes are on alert too but steps are in place.

item.title: Winter Solstice draws crowds to Newgrange
item.description: The Winter Solstice takes place this morning. Hundreds of visitors are expected to make the pilgrimage to Newgrange in Co. Meath, to see the sun illuminate the inner passage of the tomb. Only a limited number of people are allowed inside the neolithic chamber to witness the event this morning. Advertisement Leontia Lenehan, Supervisor Guide at Brú na Bóinne, says a lucky lottery winner from home and abroad will be going into the chamber.

item.title: Woman killed in Monaghan crash laid to rest today
item.description: A woman killed in a fatal road traffic collision in Co Monaghan will be laid to rest today. Tributes have been pouring in for Emma Mackeral, a mother of two from Clones, who died following a collision on the N2 on Thursday. She is being remembered as a much loved and highly respected person. Advertisement The funeral service will take place on Sunday the 21st of December at 2pm at Stonebridge Presbyterian Church, Gransha More, Clones, Co Monaghan followed by interment in the adjoining graveyard.

item.title: Local senator calls for CPR and first aid training in driver theory test
item.description: A local Senator is highlighting the need for CPR and first aid training to be included in the driver theory test. Robbie Gallagher recently raised the issue, after he was approached by the Irish Heart Foundation. The proposal would ensure learner drivers have knowledge of CPR, defibrillator use and emergency response at road traffic accidents. Advertisement It comes as similar measures are due to be introduced in the UK in early 2026, with an EU directive expected to be transposed into Irish law

item.title: Man in his 30s seriously injured in Omagh assault
item.description: A man in his 30s has been seriously injured in an assault in Omagh in County Tyrone. Police officers on patrol in the Main Street area of the town came across a man with a number of facial and head injuries at around 1 o'clock this morning. He was taken to hospital, where he's in a critical, but stable condition today. Advertisement An 18-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent, and remains in custody.

item.title: Monaghan family competes in Ireland’s Fittest Family final tonight
item.description: A Co. Monaghan family is taking part in Ireland's Fittest Family tonight. The McKenna's from Corraghbrack are a very active family who love sport. The team consists of mum Sharon, her two sons Caolan and Cormac, along with her daughter Cailin who described herself to Northern Sound as a "fitness fanatic." Advertisement The final of Ireland's Fittest Family will kick off at 6.30pm on RTÉ 1. Speaking to Northern Sound, Caolan McKenna said that he is proud of his family for what they have achieved

item.title: Cavan Eagles fall to Glanmire
item.description: UCC Glanmire recovered from a slow start, to claim a nine point win over McEvoy’s Cavan Eagles. Ealges had led by 12 in the closing stages of the opening quarter. However, the Cork side came back to secure a 94-85 win over McEvoy's Cavan Eagles on Sunday. It moves Mark Scannell's side to a 6-3 record.
